I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because at my age I care first about stability, grain for sale, and work I know how to manage well. In Quzhou County, winter wheat followed by summer maize fits the weather, the water conditions, and the machinery available around me. I would not make the year complicated with too many crops. I would keep one simple pattern across my land so I can manage fertilizer, irrigation, and pest control in a familiar way. For the winter wheat already in the field, I will focus on steady topdressing, two to three irrigations depending on moisture, and basic disease and weed control so I can protect yield without making management too hard. After wheat harvest, I will quickly seed summer maize on the same land, using hybrid seed because maize yield depends strongly on seed vigor. For maize, I will put fertilizer mainly around key growth stages, irrigate when the field is dry, and keep pesticide sprays limited to the times they are really needed. I will use rotary tillage for wheat and no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest so I can save time and catch the planting window. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield, but to get a dependable harvest with work intensity I can still handle.
